Note: Manufacturer ventilation unit (MVHR / heat recovery) products, as their manufacturers publish them.
THIS FILE IS THE CATALOGUE. SAM.Analytical owns the vocabulary - VentilationUnitTemplate,
VentilationUnitReference, VentilationUnitPerformanceTable, FlowFractionControlCurve - and the
Approved Document O selection rule. WHICH PRODUCTS EXIST is a fact about this repository, exactly as
it is for SystemEnergyCentre/CapabilityIndex.JSON, so the core library carries no manufacturer list
and adding a product here needs no change there.
EACH ENTRY IS A SERIALISED VentilationUnitTemplate. Query.VentilationUnitTemplates reads them and
then VALIDATES every one; a single unusable entry REFUSES THE WHOLE CATALOGUE rather than being
skipped, because a product silently vanishing from a library is the failure mode that produces a
smaller answer nobody notices.
CAPACITY AND PERFORMANCE ARE DIFFERENT FACTS AND ARE SOURCED SEPARATELY.
MaximumSupplyFlowRate_Lps / MaximumExtractFlowRate_Lps are what Iteration 2 selects on. The
PerformanceTable is what Iteration 3 will simulate from. AN AIRFLOW APPEARING ON A PERFORMANCE
TABLE AXIS IS A PUBLISHED DUTY POINT AND IS NEVER READ AS THE UNIT CAPACITY. A template whose
capacity is unresolved keeps its full performance data and is simply not offered to selection - see
UnresolvedCapacityNote on the entry, and Query.UnselectableVentilationUnitTemplates, which lists such
entries with the reason so that a missing product is reportable rather than invisible.
PERFORMANCE DATA IS THE MANUFACTURER RAW TABLE, NOT A DERIVED REPRESENTATION. Values are stored in
the units the source publishes them in and are never converted on the way in. Interpolation between
published conditions, and any behaviour beyond them, is applied at the point of use under an explicit
PerformanceDomainPolicy - it is not baked in here. The legacy route that preceded this file kept one
80 l/s slice of the Nuaire table and generated an equation from it; both are useful derived views and
neither is checkable against the brochure afterwards, which is why the brochure is what this file
holds.
RANK IS DECLARED LIBRARY POLICY. Lower is preferred, and it is ONLY a tie-break between products that
are the same size on both sides - size decides first. It is not derived from anything. The single
value below is provisional and orders nothing today.
FlowFractionByControlTemperature is the CONTROLLER ramp, carried as template data so that no generic
air handling unit algorithm anywhere holds a hard-coded 22 or 26. Its own PerformanceDomainPolicy is
stated on the curve: ClampToDomain, because the source says 100% at 26 degrees AND ABOVE, which is a
saturating statement rather than an assumption.
WHICH TEMPERATURE drives that controller, where one unit serves several rooms whose temperatures
differ, is an Iteration 3 control question. NOTHING HERE ANSWERS IT.

Templates.Name: Nuaire MRXBOXAB-ECO5-AECV (MR-ECO-COOL-V)
Templates.Source: Nuaire, MRXBOX Hybrid Cooling System brochure, v.1 July 2022, pages 6-7 - selection tables for MRXBOXAB-ECO5-AECV with MR-ECO-COOL-V, vertical unit. The brochure states these are TYPICAL cooling data based on sample conditions and asks that Nuaire be contacted for project-specific data. MaximumSupplyFlowRate_Lps/MaximumExtractFlowRate_Lps are read off the SAME page's 'Performance' fan static-pressure chart (Fan static pressure (Pa) vs Air volume flow rate (l/s)), NOT off the cooling-duty table below it: the chart plots three fan curves, each labelled with its power draw in the Electrical and Sound Data table (Curve 1 = 319 W, Curve 2 = 167 W, Curve 3 = 77 W), and each curve's free-air (0 Pa) endpoint is the airflow that fan-speed setting can deliver against no external resistance. Curve 1, the highest available setting, ends at 150 l/s - digitised from the chart's vector paths against its own axis calibration (0 l/s at x=689.9pt, 25 l/s per 54.7pt, page rect 1190.55x841.89pt), not estimated by eye. Curves 2 and 3 end at approximately 120 l/s and 90 l/s respectively and are not otherwise recorded here, since this schema carries one maximum per direction. This unit is a balanced heat-recovery core, so the same chart figure is used for both supply and extract; the brochure publishes one combined 'air volume flow rate', not separate supply/extract curves.
